name: people_de
items: A 16-year-old secondary-school student in Flensburg, Germany, who shares a room with her younger sister and mainly uses AI on a cracked Android phone.
A 19-year-old apprentice industrial mechanic in Chemnitz, Germany, who restores an old Simson moped and prefers short, practical explanations.
A 22-year-old nursing student in Vienna, Austria, who works weekend shifts in elder care and is the first in her family to attend university.
A 24-year-old dairy farmer in Appenzell, Switzerland, who helps run the family farm and has unreliable internet in the cowshed.
A 27-year-old unemployed retail worker in Dortmund, Germany, who is applying for retraining while caring for his three-year-old son.
A 29-year-old bicycle courier in Basel, Switzerland, who speaks German as a second language and tracks every expense in a spreadsheet.
A 31-year-old primary-school teacher in Graz, Austria, who leads an after-school chess club and is cautious about student privacy.
A 33-year-old shipyard welder in Rostock, Germany, who works rotating shifts and is planning a low-budget camping trip with friends.
A 35-year-old self-employed hairdresser in St. Pölten, Austria, who runs a two-chair salon and handles all bookings through WhatsApp.
A 37-year-old municipal clerk in Potsdam, Germany, who prepares accessible public notices and has strong knowledge of administrative procedures.
A 39-year-old hotel receptionist in Interlaken, Switzerland, who regularly writes messages in several languages but lacks confidence with formal German.
A 41-year-old single mother and supermarket cashier on Norderney, Germany, who coordinates childcare around seasonal ferry schedules.
A 43-year-old software tester in Zurich, Switzerland, who is visually impaired and relies heavily on keyboard navigation and screen readers.
A 45-year-old vineyard worker near Krems an der Donau, Austria, who records weather observations in a paper notebook and rarely uses a computer.
A 47-year-old paramedic in Augsburg, Germany, who volunteers with a local youth sports club and asks highly specific health-related questions.
A 49-year-old owner of a small Turkish-German bakery in Cologne, Germany, who experiments with sourdough and needs help wording customer announcements.
A 51-year-old carpenter in a village near Innsbruck, Austria, who builds custom staircases and learned digital invoicing only recently.
A 53-year-old social worker in Lausanne, Switzerland, who works in German and French and supports families facing housing insecurity.
A 55-year-old police administrative employee in Hanover, Germany, who enjoys genealogy and carefully distinguishes verified facts from family stories.
A 57-year-old sheep farmer in Brandenburg, Germany, who manages conservation grazing and uses a shared family laptop for official paperwork.
A 59-year-old pharmacist in Salzburg, Austria, who cares for an elderly parent and wants concise summaries backed by reliable sources.
A 61-year-old tram driver in Bern, Switzerland, who photographs urban wildlife during early shifts and is comfortable with basic apps but not file management.
A 64-year-old laid-off textile worker in the Swabian Jura, Germany, who attends evening classes and is learning to write a modern CV.
A 67-year-old retired civil engineer in Linz, Austria, who sings in a choir and enjoys checking calculations independently.
A 70-year-old former postal worker in Lugano, Switzerland, who grew up speaking Italian and now practices written German for messages to grandchildren.
A 72-year-old retired librarian in Weimar, Germany, who digitizes local-history documents and is meticulous about citations and dates.
A 75-year-old pensioner in a village in the Emmental, Switzerland, who maintains a large vegetable garden and uses voice input because of arthritis.
A 78-year-old former cleaner in Munich, Germany, who lives alone, speaks Bosnian at home and needs patient guidance for online appointments.
A 82-year-old retired ferry engineer on Rügen, Germany, who follows maritime weather reports and distrusts unfamiliar buttons on websites.
An 85-year-old former seamstress in Feldkirch, Austria, who exchanges long emails with relatives abroad and keeps printed copies of important instructions.
